_source: Multiple structural analyses: studiobinder.com, gointothestory.blcklst.com, scyn.app, and the published English-language screenplay (Bong Joon-ho and Han Jin-won, translated by Darcy Paquet, published by Grand Central Publishing 2020 ISBN 978-1538753644).
_notes: 145-page English translation. Parasite does not map cleanly onto a standard 110-page STC template — it is 145 pages and has an intentional genre-shift at the midpoint (comedy-of-cons to home-invasion thriller to tragedy). Beat positions are functional rather than strict page-count targets.
title: Parasite

beat_descriptions.Opening Image: The Kim family in their semi-basement apartment, struggling to find WiFi.
beat_descriptions.Catalyst: Min-hyuk arrives with the scholar stone and the tutoring job offer for Ki-woo.
beat_descriptions.Break Into Two: Ki-woo is hired. The family infiltration plan begins.
beat_descriptions.Midpoint: Moon-gwang returns, reveals the secret underground bunker and Geun-sae. Genre shifts from con-comedy to survival thriller.
beat_descriptions.All Is Lost: The rainstorm floods the Kim basement. The Parks return early. The situation spirals into violence.
beat_descriptions.Break Into Three: The garden party. Geun-sae emerges. Ki-jung is stabbed. The plan collapses into tragedy.
beat_descriptions.Final Image: Ki-woo reads his father Ki-taek letter from inside the Park house. The final image mirrors the opening — cramped, alone, dreaming.
